rationale: The route MESSAGE→REACTION→USER→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP is fully used and correctly maps 'role in our workspace' to user_teams (workspace membership), not channel membership. Two same-named users (Robert Walsh, admin; Robert Chen, member) genuinely create an unresolved referent with no delegated tie-breaker in the prompt, correctly justifying resolution_mode=underspecified and the two alternative candidate_role_sets for the message obligation. Both target messages (1699564800.000123, 1706000208.000000) and both memberships already exist in the base seed with correct role values; the reaction rows themselves are still to be added by the compiler, which is acceptable at the design stage per the review rules for planned additions. Negatives are well-chosen and non-hinting: wrong-emoji-by-same-reactor (tests emoji-value precision and author-vs-reactor distinction), and wrong-person-right-emoji (Sophie Dubois) correctly excluded by the name condition. Access plan (conversations.list/history, reactions.get, users.info) is realistic and the acting bot is a member of every channel needed for discovery (#general, C_INFRA, C_MODEL), so no hidden-ID or unsupported-capability problem exists. Attributes requested (message_text, channel_id, user_id, user_teams.role) are bare stored columns, matching the locked-field convention. The exposure_qualification's admin/member framing is consistent with the actual enum values present in the seed (no owner/guest confusion). This is a strong, well-motivated ambiguity test rather than a bare retrieval case.
